title: 7 thinking traps that shape your decisions

cover.headline: 7 thinking traps that shape your decisions
cover.sub: And one small fix for each

items.title: Anchoring
items.body: The first number you see becomes your reference point, even when someone else chose it.
items.try: Decide your own range before you see a price or an offer.

items.title: Confirmation bias
items.body: We tend to search for, notice and remember what agrees with what we already think.
items.try: Search for the best argument against your view once.

items.title: Sunk cost
items.body: Money or time already spent can keep us going, even when stopping would serve us better.
items.try: Ask: if I were starting today, would I choose this?

items.title: Framing
items.body: The same facts feel different depending on the wording. '90% survive' and '10% die' lead to different choices.
items.try: Restate the choice the other way before you decide.

items.title: Planning fallacy
items.body: We underestimate how long our own tasks will take, even when past tasks ran late.
items.try: Check how long the last similar task actually took.

items.title: Present bias
items.body: Rewards today feel bigger than rewards later, so 'next month' keeps winning.
items.try: Automate the decision so the future gets a default.

items.title: Illusory truth
items.body: Claims we have heard many times feel more true, even when we know better.
items.try: Ask: do I know this, or have I just heard it a lot?
items.source: Fazio et al., 2015, J Experimental Psychology: General

closing.action: Pick one trap you fall into most. Notice it once this week.
closing.kicker: Save this for your next big decision
